newsitem.title: CANADA: Brookfield raises stake in World Financial.
newsitem.headline: Brookfield raises stake in World Financial.

text.p: Brookfield Properties Corp on Friday said will spend C$220 million to increase its stake in New York-based World Financial Properties Inc by 25 percent.
The Toronto-based real estate company said after the purchase it will hold a 70 percent stake in the company, with Citibank NA holding 23 percent.

The World Financial stake is being purchased from the Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and Dragon Holdings Ltd, which held 21 percent and four percent respectively of the company. Dragon Holdings is controlled by Hong Kong financier Li Ka-Shing.

Brookfield said it will pay for the increased stake with about C$200 million in cash and the issuance of 2.9 million six year warrants of Brookfield with an exercise price of C$15 per shares. The acquisition is expected to be completed prior to July 31, 1997.

World Financial owns and operates three towers of the World Financial Center, One Liberty Plaza and 245 Park Avenue in Manhattan. Brookfield in Novmeber acquired a 46 percent interest in World Financial for an undisclosed sum, making it the company's controlling shareholder.

Brookfield said that since the initial acquisition in November, World Financial's portfolio occupancy rate has been increased to 98 percent through the leasing of more than 700,000 square feet of space.

"The acquisition will provide substantial benefits to Brookfield's shareholders in 1997 and beyond. It also adds to the stable stream of income produced by six office properties, with the average lease term of the space being acquired being over twelve years," Gordon Arnell, Brookfield's chief executive, said in a statement.

Arnell said the acquisition was consistent with Brookfield's strategy of increasing its effective ownerhip in its existing properties. The purchase increased Brookfield's ownership interest by 2.2 million square feet and would be immediately accretive to cash flows and earnings per share, Arnell said.
Once the acquisition was completed, Brookfield said it would have a net effective ownership interest in 18 million square feet of rentable area.
Brookfield is controlled by the Edper Group Ltd which is controlled by the Bronfman family of Toronto.
